findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data instead of real results
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of passing the actual fetched `result.data` / `result.meta` that are available in scope (and are used by the `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch). Any organization with this flag enabled will see an always-empty table widget regardless of the underlying query results, a functional regression for dashboard table widgets.

findings.title: Mixing millisecond and second timestamps when interleaving errors with breadcrumbs
findings.body: `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` (populated from `ErrorEvent`, sourced from the Sentry event's `data.get("timestamp")`, which is a Unix timestamp in seconds) against `event.get("timestamp", 0)` from rrweb-style breadcrumb/recording events, whose `timestamp` field is conventionally in epoch milliseconds. Comparing these directly (seconds vs. milliseconds, differing by ~1000x) will produce an incorrect chronological merge of errors and breadcrumbs in the generated log stream sent to Seer for summarization — errors will systematically sort far earlier (or later) than their true position relative to breadcrumbs. The added tests use the same unit for both values and do not exercise this mismatch, so the bug is untested.

findings.title: Fragile positional zip between error_ids and nodestore results
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, then does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and zips `error_ids` with `events.values()`. This assumes `events` is a dict that preserves the exact order of `node_ids` and contains one entry (even if None) for every requested id. If the backend's `get_multi` implementation ever omits missing keys rather than mapping them to `None`, the zip will silently misalign `error_id`s with the wrong event data for all entries after the first missing one, corrupting the summary (wrong title/message attributed to an error). Using `events.get(node_id)` per id would be safer than relying on positional correspondence via `.values()`.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature-flag check and request validation
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is called at the very top of `post()`, before the `features.has(...)` check and before the request body is validated. This means the analytics event fires even for requests from organizations without the feature enabled, and even for malformed/invalid requests that will ultimately be rejected with a 400/404, polluting usage analytics with non-successful or unauthorized attempts.

findings.title: Broad exception swallowed and logged with a raw exception object in `extra`
findings.body: `get_environment_info` catches bare `Exception` and logs via `logger.info("get_environment_info.no-environment", extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e})`, passing the exception instance itself as a value in `extra`. Depending on the logging/serialization pipeline, non-serializable values in `extra` can cause logging failures or be silently dropped; `str(e)` or `exc_info=True` should be used instead. The overly broad except also means genuine bugs in this code path (e.g., AttributeError from a code change) will be silently swallowed rather than surfaced.

findings.title: Static method references a differently-named class instead of itself/cls
findings.body: `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is a `@staticmethod` that calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` instead of `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` (or using `cls`). This only works if `PRCommentWorkflow` happens to inherit `_truncate_title` from `CommitContextIntegration`; hard-coding a differently named class inside a base-class method is fragile and will break (AttributeError) if that inheritance relationship ever changes or if this method is reused from a context where `PRCommentWorkflow` isn't in the MRO.
